title.narrative: Increasing the sustainability and resilience of agriculture/food system through nature-based solutions

description.narrative: 130. The Knowledge Management (KM) approach for FSIP Türkiye is designed to capture, organize, and disseminate lessons learned on NbS in agricultural and rangeland management. By embedding structured knowledge-sharing mechanisms into project implementation, FSIP Türkiye aims to inform decision-making, scale best practices, and contribute to regional and global knowledge frameworks. 131. A Knowledge Management System (KMS) will serve as the central repository for project insights, ensuring accessibility and usability for policymakers, farmers, and private sector actors. At least two knowledge products per year, including case studies, policy briefs, and technical reports, will be developed, with a focus on scalability and gender-responsive learning. Select case studies will also be assessed for inclusion in the WOCAT Global Sustainable Land Management (SLM) Database, aligning with international knowledge-sharing efforts. 132. To promote stakeholder engagement and peer learning, FSIP Türkiye will integrate Farmer Field Schools (FFS), digital platforms, and policy dialogues to reach at least 2,000 stakeholders. These platforms will connect government agencies, research institutions, and private sector actors to exchange best practices and foster collaboration. The project will also contribute to the FSIP Global Coordination Platform, facilitating knowledge exchange at the regional and global levels. 133. Capacity building will be a core element of the KM strategy, ensuring that NbS approaches are institutionalized in agricultural training programs. The project will develop a digital education platform to provide on-demand learning resources, complementing in-person training initiatives. 134. The communication strategy will ensure that project findings are widely disseminated through policy advocacy, public awareness campaigns, and digital outreach. High-level policy dialogues will facilitate regulatory integration of NbS, while targeted media content and stakeholder workshops will support behavioral change and adoption at different levels. A dedicated digital platform will host interactive materials, webinars, and real-time support for agribusinesses and policymakers. 135. A Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework will track the effectiveness of knowledge-sharing efforts, integrating gender-responsive indicators and adaptive learning mechanisms. Regular updates to the FSIP Global Coordination Platform will ensure that Türkiye’s experiences contribute to broader programmatic learning and inform policy developments. Year 2-4 118,768 Total 228,768 E.2 Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment Socio-economic Benefits. 136. The project delivers significant socioeconomic benefits at both national and local levels, fostering sustainable agricultural practices, enhancing livelihoods, and building resilience to climate change. At the national level, the integration of Nature-based Solutions (NbS) improves agricultural productivity by enhancing soil fertility, optimizing water use, and conserving biodiversity. These interventions lead to higher crop and livestock yields, strengthening food security and reducing Türkiye's reliance on imports. Additionally, the development of market systems for NbS products, including eco-certification and value chain integration, increases farmers’ profitability and reduces their vulnerability to economic shocks. By aligning these sustainable practices with national policies and governance frameworks, the project strengthens institutional capacity and promotes long-term policy coherence in agricultural and environmental management. 137. At the local level, the project empowers smallholder farmers and rural communities through targeted training, financial incentives, and access to sustainable technologies. Gender-responsive approaches ensure the inclusion of women and marginalized groups in decision-making processes, training programs, and governance mechanisms, fostering equitable economic growth. By adopting climate adaptation measures such as improved water management systems and resilient crop varieties, local communities are better equipped to manage climate shocks, secure their livelihoods, and enhance overall resilience. 138. These socioeconomic benefits contribute directly to global environmental goals. Improved agricultural productivity and market systems reduce pressures on natural ecosystems, curbing land conversion and preserving biodiversity. Sustainable practices, such as conservation agriculture and integrated water management, enhance carbon sequestration and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, aligning with GEF Trust Fund priorities for climate mitigation. The restoration of degraded lands and the promotion of NbS also support Türkiye’s commitments to land degradation neutrality under the Rio Conventions. Decent Rural Employment 139. The project promotes full and productive employment by generating sustainable livelihoods in rural areas through Nature-based Solutions (NbS). It enhances technical skills and market access for farmers, creating opportunities in ecosystem restoration, sustainable farming, and value chain development. 140. Aligned with the FAO’s Decent Rural Employment (DRE) guidelines, the project ensures safe working conditions, fair wages, and the inclusion of women and marginalized groups through its Gender Action Plan. Training and capacity-building programs empower rural workers while promoting compliance with labor standards. By linking rural producers to premium markets and fostering partnerships with the private sector, the project ensures long-term sustainability, contributing to inclusive rural development and poverty reduction.
